keyVerseText: I am weary with my groaning; all the night make I my bed to swim; I water my couch with my tears. all: or, every night
rootMeaning: The Hebrew verb שָׂחָה (sâchâh) is a primitive root primarily meaning 'to swim' or 'to cause to swim.' Its core sense involves movement through water, either by oneself or by causing another to do so. This literal image of immersion and flowing movement adds depth beyond the simple English gloss of 'swim,' suggesting a dynamic interaction with water that can imply inundation or being overwhelmed.
usageInScripture: The word appears three times in the Hebrew Bible, consistently related to the concept of swimming or causing to swim. The top translations include 'his hands to swim' twice and simply 'to swim' once, indicating a focus on the physical act of swimming or being immersed. This usage range highlights both the literal and causative aspects of the verb, showing its application from physical movement to metaphorical inundation.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding שָׂחָה as 'to swim' or 'to inundate' enriches our grasp of biblical imagery where water often symbolizes chaos, distress, or overwhelming circumstances. In the Christian faith, this root evokes the believer's experience of being submerged in trials yet sustained by God's presence. The causative form, 'to make to swim,' can reflect God's sovereign control over situations that might otherwise engulf us, reminding us that He directs even the floods of life. This word thus deepens our appreciation for God's sustaining grace amid life's storms.
keyVerseReflection: In Psalms 6:6, the psalmist laments, 'I am weary with my groaning; all the night make I my bed to swim; I water my couch with my tears.' Here, שָׂחָה conveys the image of the bed being flooded or soaked with tears, vividly expressing deep sorrow and emotional overwhelm. The verb intensifies the sense of distress, portraying the psalmist as immersed in grief, which invites believers to bring their burdens honestly before God, trusting in His compassionate care.
